info.name: Digital Onboarding Service
info.description:
Customer onboarding and remote account opening APIs.

Folders:
1. Happy Path - full register/login/overview flow
2. Negative - Registration
3. Negative - Login
4. Negative - Authorization
5. Rate Limiter (legacy DB protection)

IMPORTANT: the service caps traffic at 2 requests/second globally. A collection-level pre-request script paces requests so the functional tests do not trip the limiter. The rate limiter folder deliberately bypasses that pacing.

// tests are not throttled by traffic from earlier tests.

item.name: 5. Rate Limiter
item.description: The legacy DB is protected by a global 2 req/sec limit enforced in ApiRateLimitFilter. These requests deliberately burst past the limit using pm.sendRequest, which bypasses the collection-level pacing script.

exec: // Fire a rapid burst at /overview and record every status code.
// Requests are sequential but fast on localhost, so they land in the
// same one-second window and trip the limiter.
// An invalid token is used on purpose: the filter runs BEFORE the
// controller, so allowed requests return 401 and throttled ones 429.
// That difference is exactly what we assert on.
// The burst just exhausted the budget. Tell the pacer so the next
// request waits instead of inheriting a spent window.
const allowed = statuses.filter(function (s) { return s !== 429 && s !== 0; });
